summary: The narrator, who is recovering in a clinic and feeling shaky, is told by a doctor practicing 'holistic' medicine that they are virtually certain of something, leaving the narrator to decide whether to continue the program. The narrator plans to collect their things and leave, and asks whether their Blue Cross covers the care, receiving the reply that it is on the house. In a dark room, a childlike young woman with braided hair and red glass beads says the narrator is 'special' and offers a baggie of herbal powders to be boiled and drunk daily for a week, which the narrator sets aside while growing suspicious.
one_line: A recovering narrator leaves a holistic clinic and is pressed by a young woman to take herbal powders, growing wary of the place.
key_facts: The narrator has mixed feelings about the doctor's 'holistic' medicine.
The doctor tells the narrator he is 'virtually certain' about something and that continuing the program is the narrator's own decision.
The narrator says they will get their things now and talk more about the program when feeling better.
The narrator asks whether their Blue Cross covers the clinic, and the doctor answers 'On the house.'
The narrator's clothes are in a room with a closet in the corner by the window.
A large white door appears to lead to another wing of the clinic.
The narrator hears a shuffling sound in the room and finds it dark, because somebody has closed the Venetian blinds.
A short woman, childlike but probably mid-twenties, has dark hair done in multiple braids with a red glass bead at the end of each.
The young woman says 'You're special. We all know it. That's why he brought you over here, to this building.'
The young woman carries a fanny pack and a baggie of plastic vials containing herbs she says she has started growing at the clinic.
The narrator wears black jeans and struggles into them while being pressed to take the herbs.
The herbs are gray and green powders and flakes in clear plastic medicine bottles.
The young woman instructs the narrator to put two teaspoons of each herb in boiled water and drink it every day for a week.
The narrator tells her 'I'm going to be just fine, really' and sets the baggie aside.

entities.name: Blue Cross
entities.role: health insurer the narrator asks about coverage for the clinic care

entities.name: Ramala
entities.role: attendant who shuts down the clinic equipment
